facts.statement: Xiaosaurus was a small, herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic in what is now the Sichuan Basin of China.
facts.quote: Xiaosaurus ("dawn lizard", ), is a genus of small herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur from the middle Jurassic (approximately 170.3 to 163.5 million years ago) of what is now the Sichuan Basin of China.

facts.statement: The animal lived approximately 170.3 to 163.5 million years ago in the Sichuan Basin of China.
facts.quote: Xiaosaurus ("dawn lizard", ), is a genus of small herbivorous ornithischian dinosaur from the middle Jurassic (approximately 170.3 to 163.5 million years ago) of what is now the Sichuan Basin of China.

facts.statement: Two specimens of Xiaosaurus were discovered in 1979 and 1980 during excavations near Dashanpu in Sichuan.
facts.quote: In 1979 and 1980, two specimens were discovered of a small herbivorous dinosaur during excavations near Dashanpu in Sichuan.

facts.statement: Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu named the type species Xiaosaurus dashanpensis in 1983.
facts.quote: In 1983 Dong Zhiming and Tang Zilu named the fossils under the type species Xiaosaurus dashanpensis.

facts.statement: The generic name Xiaosaurus means "dawn lizard" and references the age of the fossil.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Chinese xiáo, 曉, "dawn", a reference to the age of the fossil.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the lower Xiashaximiao Formation, where the age is uncertain but proposed to be either Bajocian or Bathonian–Callovian.
facts.quote: The holotype, IVPP V6730A, was found in the lower Xiashaximiao Formation of which the age is uncertain: both the Bajocian and the Bathonian–Callovian have been proposed.

facts.statement: The femur of Xiaosaurus is 11 centimeters long.
The original describers classified Xiaosaurus in both the Fabrosauridae and Hypsilophodontidae families, viewing it as an evolutionary link between Lesothosaurus and Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: The describers assigned it both to the Fabrosauridae and the Hypsilophodontidae, considering it an evolutionary link between Lesothosaurus and Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Xiaosaurus is a valid species or a nomen dubium with uncertain affinities, possibly belonging to basal cerapods or marginocephalians.
facts.quote: Xiaosaurus has sometimes been considered a nomen dubium and an ornithischian of uncertain affinities, possibly a basal cerapod or marginocephalian.

facts.statement: Paul Barrett et al. concluded in 2005 that Xiaosaurus is provisionally valid because it possesses a unique autapomorphy: a mediolaterally straight humerus.
facts.quote: However, Paul Barrett et al. in 2005 concluded it to be provisionally valid, as it possessed a single unique derived trait or autapomorphy: a mediolaterally (seen from the front) straight humerus.

facts.statement: Xiaosaurus dashanpensis is the only known species of the extinct Xiaosaurus genus, a basal ornithischian dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 168 to 161 million years ago.
facts.quote: Xiaosaurus dashanpensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Xiaosaurus (zhn. "pequeño lagarto") de dinosaurio ornitisquio basal, que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 168 a 161 millones de años, desde el Bathoniense al Calloviense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the lower Xiashaximiao Formation, where the age is uncertain with proposals ranging from Bajocian to Bathonian–Callovian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, IVPP V6730A, se encontró en la Formación Xiashaximiao inferior, cuya edad es incierta: se han propuesto tanto el Bajociense como el Bathoniense al Calloviense.

facts.statement: The paratype specimen includes a partial skeleton with a right femur, a dorsal vertebra, two sacral vertebrae, a phalanx, a rib, and two teeth.
facts.quote: El paratipo IVPP V6730B es un segundo esqueleto parcial que incluye un fémur derecho, una vértebra dorsal, dos vértebras sacras, una falange, una costilla y dos dientes.

facts.statement: In 1992, Peng Guangzhao renamed Agilisaurus multidens as Xiaosaurus multidens, but this classification has not been accepted.
facts.quote: En 1992, Peng Guangzhao cambió el nombre de Agilisaurus multidens He & Cai 1983, ahora Hexinlusaurus a una segunda especie de Xiaosaurus, Xiaosaurus multidens, pero esto no ha sido aceptado.

facts.statement: Paul Barrett et al. concluded in 2005 that the genus was provisionally valid due to a unique autapomorphy: a mediolaterally straight humerus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Paul Barrett et al. en 2005 concluyó que era válido provisionalmente, ya que poseía un único rasgo derivado único o autapomorfia, un húmero recto mediolateralmente, visto desde el frente.

facts.statement: The time range for Xiaosaurus is estimated from the Bajocian to the Oxfordian, spanning 170.9 to 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Oxfordian (170.9 to 154.8 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Xiaosaurus was a small bipedal animal with an estimated length of 1 m.
